requirement_text.REQ-067: Port src/api/pagination.zig (406 lines, R-Co's API-06) as Letflow.Api.Pagination -- the shared cursor encode/decode, prefix validation, expiry checking, page-size validation, and standardised page response that every S4 list endpoint delegates to. Port the constants exactly: MAX_PAGE_SIZE 200, DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE 50, MIN_PAGE_SIZE 1, CURSOR_EXPIRY_US 86_400_000_000. A requested page size above MAX_PAGE_SIZE, below MIN_PAGE_SIZE, or non-numeric is a 400, not a silent clamp. A cursor carries a type prefix so a cursor minted by one endpoint cannot be replayed against another. An expired cursor is rejected. SECURITY (INV-1, INV-5): the decoded cursor struct must have no tenant/schema field -- tenant scoping comes exclusively from REQ-072's future resolved request context, never from the cursor.

task.description:
Gate CODE-DESIGNER's design for `Letflow.Api.Pagination` in `lib/letflow/design/api-pagination.md` (commit `1fa6934` on `feature/WF02-REQ067-20260821`). Read the actual design doc in full -- do not read CODE-DESIGNER's own `result.summary` as a substitute. Read R-Co's real source at `C:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\src\api\pagination.zig` yourself to verify the port claims.

CHECKS, RE-DERIVE EACH:

1. EVERY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION on REQ-067 (six of them, listed below) maps to a concrete design element -- no TBD, no deferral language.
2. FUNCTION SIGNATURES fully specified: names, input/output types, error-tuple shapes for every function (`parse_page_size_param/1`, `validate_page_size/1`, `decode_cursor/4`, `encode_cursor/1`, `build_raw_cursor/3`, `build_raw_cursor_timestamp_key/4`, `parse_int_from_cursor/3`, `find_nth_colon/2`, `page_response/2`, and any accessor functions for the four constants).
3. REJECT-NOT-CLAMP CLAIM. The design claims R-Co's `validatePageSize/1` rejects (never clamps) page sizes of 0 or >200. Verify this yourself directly against the real Zig source -- do not trust the design doc's own citation.
4. THE TWO FLAGGED DIVERGENCES. CODE-DESIGNER flagged two divergences from R-Co rather than silently resolving them: (a) using an HTTP 400 for page-size rejection where `pagination.zig`'s own doc comment says 422 -- the requirement's own text explicitly asked for 400, so confirm the design followed the higher-precedence source (`context.requirement_text`) correctly; (b) splitting a new `:invalid_cursor` atom out of `:invalid_base64` for malformed-timestamp-slice failures that Zig conflates under one error -- confirm this is genuinely behaviorally equivalent (both still produce a 400) and not a silent behavior change.
5. INV-1 STRUCTURAL TRUTH. Confirm the `Cursor` type/struct genuinely has no field capable of carrying a tenant id, schema name, or scope-widening value -- read the exact struct/type definition in the design, not just the prose claiming it. Confirm the design states, explicitly and specifically, that a future endpoint's store/list function must derive tenant scope only from REQ-072's request context, never from the decoded cursor.

WHERE THE NON-NUMERIC PAGE-SIZE CHECK LIVES. CODE-DESIGNER put it in a new parse-time function (`parse_page_size_param/1`) separate from `validate_page_size/1`'s range check, reasoning Elixir has no equivalent to Zig's compile-time `?u16` type boundary. Judge whether this split is the right shape or introduces an awkward seam a route handler must compose correctly every time -- state your judgement, it does not need to be a FAIL either way as long as the design gives a complete, unambiguous composition example (check §0.1 for one).

6. NO `.ex` IMPLEMENTATION BODY present -- signatures, types, prose only.
7. DB/SCHEMA: confirm the design states plainly that no new Ecto schema or migration is needed (this module has no persistence of its own) -- absence of a DB section should be a deliberate statement, not a silent gap.

SCOPE OF `result.issues`: FAIL immediately on any check failure per WF-02's own Step 1b procedure -- no partial credit. Non-blocking notes still get recorded, not silently dropped.

VERDICT: PASS or FAIL against WF-02 Step 1b's standard checklist plus the items above. A FAIL names every failed check by requirement id, per the workflow's own validator-fail convention. Commit your own handoff file to this branch. Do not write `registry.json` or `orchestrator.log`.
